title: Embed ingress shaping and slot-packing experiments for P99 reduction
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background: Customer-facing vector endpoints show p99 spikes during mixed-size batches and bursty ingress. Previous work focused on kernel hints and prefetch; this ticket explores ingress shaping (request ingress windowing) paired with slot-packing (GPU slot occupancy-aware request packing) to reduce straggler amplification without harming median latency or embedding quality.

Goals: 1) Reduce embed p99 by 20–40% for typical traffic profiles; 2) Keep p50 within +5ms of baseline; 3) Avoid quality regressions and preserve throughput.

Hypothesis: Short deterministic ingress windows (1–5ms) combined with a fast slot packing heuristic (pack requests with similar seq_len and model_variant into execution slots) will reduce tail amplification caused by uneven GPU occupancy and oversized microbatches.

Plan:
- Build an ingress-shaper shim in front of vector endpoints that buffers up to X requests or Y ms (configurable).
- Implement an occupancy-aware slot-packing policy in the request coalescer: group by seq_len bucket and quantization profile, prefer tight-fill to reduce kernel padding.
- Add lightweight telemetry: per-window batch size histograms, slot utilization, kernel call durations, and correlation between ingress window and p99.
- Run controlled A/B in staging with production-sampled traffic (replay and live canary) and collect p50/p95/p99, QPS, throughput, and token cost.
- Evaluate interactions with KV cache hit rates and prefix caching.

Success criteria: 20–40% p99 reduction on >90% of traffic slices with <=2% throughput loss. Rollback if p99 or customer-facing errors increase >5% or if cost increases >8% without latency benefit.

Trade-offs & Risks: Small ingress windows add latency for some requests; slot-packing heuristic could increase variance for very short sequences. Kernel inversion problems may surface for rare model variants; will add guardrails to disable packing for flagged variants.

Artifacts: design doc with measurement plan + experiment dashboard (links below).

Next steps: code prototype for ingress shim, unit tests for packing heuristic, instrumentation, run 48h replay experiments, review with runtime owners, schedule canary rollout.
